summary.name: Unshaky
summary.one_liner: Unshaky is a macOS utility that filters out accidental "double key press" input from the butterfly-keyboard MacBooks by ignoring keystrokes that arrive within a set delay after the previous one.
use_cases: Stop double letters caused by a faulty butterfly keyboard
Avoid paying for a keyboard replacement on an older MacBook
Filter out accidental repeated keystrokes on macOS
Tune a per-key delay for fast typing
summary.what_it_does: The app ignores any key press that occurs no later than a configurable number of milliseconds after the previous effective key press. Users open the menu bar icon and choose Configure to set delays for the defective keys. The author suggests starting around 40 ms and increasing gradually, since a long delay can block legitimate fast double letters. The page says the source code is on GitHub, that it sends no user information or keyboard records, and that anyone can audit or build it. It requires Accessibility permission and can be added to Login Items to run at startup.
notable: Source code on GitHub, auditable and buildable by anyone
Configurable per-key delay in milliseconds, set from the menu bar
States it collects no user information or keystroke records
Targets MacBook butterfly keyboards (MacBook, MacBook Air 2018, MacBook Pro 2016 and later)
caveats: Page says it reportedly stopped working on macOS 10.15.6 unless set to default, with a workaround linked in an issue
Needs Accessibility permission (and Input Monitoring is not enough on Catalina)
A long delay can block legitimate fast repeated letters such as the 'pp' in apple
Page is largely dated (references 2018-2020 Apple service programs)
